mainTopic: מוקצה rulings, רב חסדא's practical advice to students and to his daughters, and a משנה about handling animal feed on שבת
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing some rulings about מוקצה. You may slide an item off a plain reed but not move the reed, though a weaver's tool may be moved. A bundle of vegetables may be moved if animals can eat it, and a meat hook may be moved but a fish hook may not. רב קטינא's comparison about standing in the middle of a bed is rejected. Next comes a long series of practical advice from רב חסדא to poor Torah students: how to buy vegetables, reeds, meat and a linen shirt wisely, how to handle a little bread, and how to protect their clothes and their dignity. Along the way, the גמרא rejects the idea that eating better food violates בל תשחית, because caring for one's body comes first. רב חסדא also teaches his daughters modest behavior toward their husbands, ending with a lesson acted out with a pearl and a clod of earth. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and notes that it does not follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. A new משנה follows about clearing feed before animals. The גמרא shows that the חכמים disagree with both of רבי דוסא's cases, and that the dispute is only about a trough that is a vessel. Finally, אביי resolves two conflicting ברייתות about moving feed between animals, and his explanation continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Slide the item off the reed, but do not take the reed off the item
steps.stepSummary: This עמוד opens partway through a ruling from the previous עמוד. An item is hanging on a reed. Pulling the item off the reed is permitted. Pulling the reed out of the item is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: To pull it off the reed is permitted; to pull the reed out of it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling that began on the previous עמוד, about an item hanging on a reed on שבת. It explains which object you may move and which you may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reed is not a כלי (utensil). It has no use of its own, so it is מוקצה and may not be moved directly. The hanging item is fine to move, so you may slide it off and leave the reed where it is.

keyTerms.meaning: an item set aside from use, which may not be moved on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Both actions separate the item from the reed, so they can look the same. The difference is which object your hand is moving. Moving the permitted item is fine. Moving the reed, which is מוקצה, is not.

phrases.english: to slide it off the reed is permitted,
phrases.notes: You move the item itself, which is allowed.

phrases.english: but to pull the reed out of it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The reed is not a utensil, so it is מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁלְפָא לְדִידַהּ מִקַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling that began on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may move the permitted item off the reed, but you may not move the reed, because it is מוקצה.

steps.title: If the item hangs on a weaver's tool, that is allowed too
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a case. If the item is hanging on a weaver's tool instead of a plain reed, you may pull the tool out as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And if it is a weaver's tool, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the previous ruling. The ban on removing the reed does not apply when the item hangs on a real tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A weaver's tool is a real כלי, even though weaving is forbidden on שבת. A כלי whose main job is forbidden work (כְּלִי שֶׁמְּלַאכְתּוֹ לְאִסּוּר) is not fully מוקצה like a plain reed. So the tool may be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: a utensil whose main use is forbidden work on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic idea in הלכות מוקצה. A real כלי, even one used for forbidden work, has a more lenient status than an object that is not a כלי at all.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And if it is a weaver's tool, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: A real utensil, so removing it is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְאִם כְּלִי קִיוָּאֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the reed ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the item hangs on a weaver's tool, which is a real כלי, removing the tool is permitted.

steps.title: A bundle of vegetables depends on whether animals can eat it
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a bundle of vegetables may be moved on שבת if it is fit for animal food. If not, it may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This bundle of vegetables, if it is fit for animal food, it is permitted to move it; and if not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new, separate ruling starts here. רב חסדא gives a test for whether a bundle of vegetables may be moved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item that has some use, even only as food for animals, is not מוקצה. If the bundle is useless even for animals, it is set aside and may not be moved.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This bundle of vegetables,

phrases.aramaic: אִי חַזְיָא לְמַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה — שְׁרֵי לְטַלְטוֹלַהּ,
phrases.english: if it is fit for animal food, it is permitted to move it,
and if not, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הַאי כִּישְׁתָּא דְיַרְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the same list of מוקצה rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vegetable bundle may be moved only if it is fit for animal food.

steps.title: A meat hook may be moved, but a fish hook may not
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי quotes רב: a hook for hanging meat may be moved on שבת, but a hook for hanging fish may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: This hook, if it is for meat, it is permitted to move it; if it is for fish, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Another new ruling about moving a common household object. רב makes a distinction between two kinds of hooks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A meat hook can also be used for other things, so it counts as a usable כלי. A fish hook smells bad, and people keep it only for fish, so they mentally set it aside and it becomes מוקצה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
This hook,
if it is for meat, it is permitted to move it,
phrases.notes: It can also be used for other things.

phrases.english: if it is for fish, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: It smells bad and is kept only for fish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב: הַאי תַּלְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another separate מוקצה ruling in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A meat hook may be moved. A fish hook is מוקצה.

steps.title: Standing in the middle of a bed is compared to standing on a woman's stomach
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא says that someone who stands in the middle of a bed is like someone standing on a woman's stomach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: One who stands in the middle of the bed is as though he stands on the stomach of a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב קטינא gives a vivid comparison about standing on the middle of a bed. This sets up the גמרא's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the גאונים, the point is damage. Just as stepping on a woman's stomach would surely hurt her, stepping in the weak middle of a bed would surely break it.

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said:
One who stands in the middle of the bed,
is as though he stands on the stomach of a woman.
phrases.notes: The גאונים explain that he will surely break the bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא: הָעוֹמֵד בָּאֶמְצַע הַמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, unrelated statement in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Standing on the middle of a bed is treated as certain to cause damage.

steps.title: The גמרא rejects רב קטינא's statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא comments that רב קטינא's statement is not correct and is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is not a correct matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא itself pushes back on רב קטינא and says his statement should not be followed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase ולאו מילתא היא is a short, flat rejection. No proof is given. The statement is simply not accepted as הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: and it is not a correct matter, meaning the statement is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The rulings here turn on whether an object counts as a usable item: a plain reed is not a כלי, and a fish hook is set aside because it smells and serves only fish, so both are מוקצה. A weaver's tool, a meat hook, and vegetables fit for animals may be moved. רב קטינא's bed statement is rejected.

phrases.english: And it is not a correct matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב קטינא's statement from step 5.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The גמרא names no specific flaw. It simply says the statement is not accepted.

steps.title: Buy long vegetables because the price is set by the bundle
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא advises a poor student to buy long vegetables, because bundles are priced by thickness and the extra length comes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: A Torah student who buys vegetables should buy long ones. A bundle is a bundle, and the length comes on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The topic of a bundle of vegetables in step 3 leads the גמרא to more statements by רב חסדא. This first one is money-saving advice for a poor student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vegetable bundles are tied to a standard thickness and sold at a set price. Long vegetables cost the same as short ones, so the buyer gets the extra length for free.

keyTerms.meaning: A student of a Torah academy

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:
A Torah student who buys vegetables
should buy long ones,
a bundle is a bundle,
phrases.notes: Bundles are a standard thickness at a standard price.

phrases.english: and the length comes on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בַּר בֵּי רַב דְּזָבֵין יַרְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Associative link: step 3 was רב חסדא on a bundle of vegetables, so more of his sayings about bundles follow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor student should buy long vegetables, since the bundle price stays the same and the length is free.

steps.title: Buy long reeds for the same reason
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא gives the same advice for reeds: buy long ones, since you pay by the bundle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: A Torah student who buys reeds should buy long ones. A bundle is a bundle, and the length comes on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא applies the same money-saving rule to reeds, which people used for building or for fuel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is the same as in step 7. Reed bundles are priced by thickness, so longer reeds give more material for the same price.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:
A Torah student who buys reeds
should buy long ones,
a bundle is a bundle,
and the length comes on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בַּר בֵּי רַב דְּזָבֵין קַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel case using the same reasoning as step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor student should buy long reeds, since the length comes free.

steps.title: A student short on bread should not eat vegetables
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says a student who has little bread should avoid vegetables, because they make you hungrier.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: A Torah student who does not have much bread should not eat vegetables, because they whet the appetite.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives eating advice to a poor student. Vegetables increase appetite, which is bad for someone without enough food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not the vegetable itself. Vegetables make a person want more bread, and a poor student has no extra bread to satisfy that hunger.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּר בֵּי רַב [דְּלָא נְפִישָׁא לֵיהּ רִיפְתָּא] —
phrases.english: A Torah student [who does not have much bread]
should not eat vegetables,
because it whets the appetite.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בַּר בֵּי רַב דְּלָא נְפִישָׁא לֵיהּ רִיפְתָּא לָא לֵיכוֹל יַרְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from buying vegetables to whether a poor student should eat them at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student short on bread should avoid vegetables because they increase hunger.

steps.title: רב חסדא never ate vegetables, whether poor or rich
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא describes his own habit. He avoided vegetables when poor because they whet the appetite, and when rich because he preferred meat and fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: I did not eat vegetables when I was poor, and I did not eat vegetables when I was rich. When poor, because they whet the appetite. When rich, because I said: where a vegetable would go in, let meat and fish go in.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא backs up his advice with his own life story. He also adds a second reason for avoiding vegetables that applies once a person can afford better food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His poverty reason matches step 9. His wealth reason is new: stomach space is limited, so it is better to fill it with more nourishing food like meat and fish.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:
I did not eat vegetables in my poverty,
nor did I eat vegetables in my wealth.
In my poverty, because it whets the appetite.
In my wealth, because I said:
where a vegetable would enter,
let meat and fish enter instead.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֲנָא לָא בַּעֲנִיּוּתִי אֲכַלִי יַרְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Personal example that supports step 9 and adds a second reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא avoided vegetables in poverty because they whet the appetite, and in wealth to leave room for meat and fish.

steps.title: A student short on bread should not cut it into small slices
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא advises a poor student not to break his little bread into small pieces. He should eat it in one go.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: A Torah student who does not have much bread should not cut it into small slices.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives another tip about handling a small amount of bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating many small pieces stretches the meal out but does not satisfy. Eating what he has in one helping fills a poor student more.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּר בֵּי רַב דְּלָא נְפִישָׁא לֵיהּ רִיפְתָּא —
phrases.english: A Torah student who does not have much bread
should not cut it into small slices.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בַּר בֵּי רַב דְּלָא נְפִישָׁא לֵיהּ רִיפְתָּא לָא לִיבְצַע בַּצּוֹעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further advice for the same poor student, now about bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student short on bread should eat it in one helping rather than in small slices.

steps.title: A student short on bread should not break bread for others
steps.stepSummary: In a bracketed statement, רב חסדא says a poor student should not be the one to break bread for the table.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: A Torah student who does not have much bread should not break bread for others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar-sounding saying, shown in parentheses in the text. This one is about breaking bread to share with guests, and the next step asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is almost the same as step 11, but it drops the word בצועי. Here the point is serving others, not how the student eats for himself.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a repeat of step 11. Step 11 is about slicing your own bread. This step is about breaking bread for other people.

phrases.english: (And Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּר בֵּי רַב דְּלָא נְפִישָׁא לֵיהּ רִיפְתָּא —
phrases.english: A Torah student who does not have much bread
should not break bread for others.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בַּר בֵּי רַב דְּלָא נְפִישָׁא לֵיהּ רִיפְתָּא לָא לִיבְצַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel statement about bread, now about serving others.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor student should not be the one to break bread for others.

steps.title: Why should he not break bread for others?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind step 12.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a poor student should not break bread for others. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking bread for guests is normally an honor. So the גמרא wants to know why a poor student should skip it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a poor student should not break bread for others.

steps.title: Because he will not do it generously
steps.stepSummary: A poor student worried about his bread will break small, stingy pieces, so it is better that he not serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he will not do it with a generous eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13. A poor person will hand out small pieces, which looks stingy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he is worried about running out, he cannot serve with a generous spirit. Someone else should break the bread so the guests are treated properly.

phrases.english: Because he will not do it generously.)

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא עָבֵיד בְּעַיִן יָפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A poor person cannot break bread generously, so he should not be the one serving.

steps.title: רב חסדא checked he had enough before breaking bread
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that in his early poor days he would not break bread until he felt through the whole basket and knew he had enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: In the beginning, I would not break bread until I put my hand into the whole basket and found there all that I needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא ends this series with his own practice. He made sure there was enough bread before he started breaking it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to steps 12–14. By checking first that he had enough, he could break bread generously and not be stingy.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's advice for a poor student: get the most for your money, avoid foods that make you hungrier, eat your little bread in one helping, and only break bread for others when you can do it generously.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:
Originally, I would not break bread
until I placed my hand in the entire basket,
and found [in it all that I needed].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֲנָא מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא הֲוַאי בָּצַעְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Personal practice showing how he avoided the stinginess problem from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא only broke bread after confirming he had enough, so he could serve generously.

steps.title: Eating wheat bread when barley would do is wasteful
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that a person who could eat cheaper barley bread but eats expensive wheat bread violates בל תשחית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: Someone who is able to eat barley bread but eats wheat bread violates the prohibition of 'Do not destroy.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives another money-saving rule. Spending extra on wheat bread when barley bread would be enough counts as wasteful destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל תשחית usually means wrecking something useful, like cutting down a fruit tree. רב חסדא stretches it to cover spending money you didn't need to spend. Paying more for a fancier food is treated like throwing money away.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
Someone who is able
to eat barley bread
and eats wheat bread
violates the prohibition of 'Do not destroy.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of רב חסדא's frugality teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Choosing wheat bread when barley bread is available is a violation of בל תשחית.

steps.title: Drinking wine when beer would do is wasteful
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא makes the same point about drinks: choosing wine over cheaper beer violates בל תשחית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said: Someone who is able to drink beer but drinks wine violates the prohibition of 'Do not destroy.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a parallel rule about drinks. Spending on wine when beer is available is also called wasteful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same idea as רב חסדא's, applied to drinks instead of bread. In Babylonia beer was cheap and common, while wine was costly. Together these two statements build one view that the גמרא will now examine.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said:
Someone who is able to drink beer
and drinks wine
violates the prohibition of 'Do not destroy.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 16, applying the same principle to drinks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Choosing wine when beer is available is a violation of בל תשחית.

steps.title: Rejected: caring for your body comes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects these statements. Not harming your own body is the more important בל תשחית.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is not correct. The 'Do not destroy' of one's own body is more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on steps 16 and 17. It says eating better food is not wasteful, because it is good for your body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not deny that wasting money is בל תשחית. It points out that the same principle also applies to your body. Weakening yourself with poorer food is a bigger 'destruction' than spending a bit more money, so the better food wins.
steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling: protecting your body's health takes priority over saving money. Eating better food is not called wasteful.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying בל תשחית doesn't apply to money. It is saying that when the two clash, the body's בל תשחית outweighs the money's בל תשחית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a lasting principle: one's health is not to be sacrificed for the sake of thrift.

phrases.english: But this is not correct;
'Do not destroy' of the body is more important.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the view in steps 16 and 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects both רב חסדא's (step 16) and רב פפא's (step 17) application of בל תשחית to choosing better food and drink.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They ignored that harming one's own body is also בל תשחית, and that one outweighs saving money.

steps.title: No oil? Use ditch water
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא advises a poor student without oil to rub himself with ditch water instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: A student of the study hall who has no oil should rub himself with ditch water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a cheap substitute for oil, which people used to smear on their skin. A poor student can use ditch water instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smearing oil on the body was normal skin care, but oil cost money. The film or scum on standing ditch water works similarly, so the student gets the benefit for free.

keyTerms.meaning: A student of the study hall

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּר בֵּי רַב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ מִשְׁחָא —
phrases.english: A student of the study hall who has no oil
should rub himself with ditch water.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב חסדא's practical tips for poor students.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor student without oil may use ditch water as a substitute.

steps.title: Buy neck meat for variety
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא advises a poor student buying meat to buy from the neck, since it has three kinds of meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: A student of the study hall who buys meat should buy the neck, because it has three kinds of meat in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a meat-buying tip. The neck is a smart purchase because it gives several kinds of meat in one cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor student can't afford many different cuts. The neck contains different textures (like meat, fat, and gristle) together, so with one purchase he gets the variety of three types.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
A student of the study hall who buys meat
should buy the neck,
because it has three kinds of meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practical tip in the same series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor student should buy neck meat, which offers three kinds of meat in one cut.

steps.title: How to make a linen shirt last a year
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא advises buying a linen shirt from נהר אבא and washing it only every thirty days, guaranteeing it will last twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: A student who buys a linen shirt should buy it from נהר אבא and wash it every thirty days, so that it lasts him the twelve months of the year. And I guarantee it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives clothing advice. Buy good linen from a known source and don't over-wash it, and it will last the whole year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two tips are packed together: buy quality from the right place (נהר אבא was known for good linen), and wash only monthly, since frequent washing wears out the fabric. רב חסדא personally guarantees the result.

keyTerms.meaning: The river Abba, a place known for linen

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
A student of the study hall who buys a linen shirt
should buy it from the river Abba,
and should wash it every thirty days,
so that it lasts him the twelve months of the year,
and I guarantee it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next tip in רב חסדא's series, now about clothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buy linen from נהר אבא and wash it monthly so it lasts a full year.

steps.title: What does the word כיתוניתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word כיתוניתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'כיתוניתא'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask about a word from step 21. It is setting up an explanation of the name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge to רב חסדא's advice. It is a word question, asking what the name of the garment hints at.

phrases.english: What is 'kitonita'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״כִּיתּוֹנִיתָא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a key word used in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning or wordplay behind the term כיתוניתא.

steps.title: A fine class of people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains כיתוניתא as כיתא נאה, a fine class, since good clothing lets one fit in with respectable people.
steps.simpleTranslation: A fine class.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a wordplay. כיתוניתא sounds like כיתא נאה, 'a fine group.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name hints at why a nice shirt matters. Wearing fine clothing lets a person join a respectable class of people, so it is worth buying a good one even on a tight budget.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine class or group of people

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's tips teach a poor student to be thrifty in smart ways (ditch water, neck meat, careful washing), but the גמרא still values health and a dignified appearance.

phrases.english: A fine class.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּיתָּא נָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the word question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כיתוניתא is read as כיתא נאה, since fine clothing brings one into a respectable class.

steps.title: A student should not sit on a new mat
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא advises a בר בי רב not to sit on a new mat, because it ruins his clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: A Torah student should not sit on a new mat, because it ruins his clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives another practical money-saving tip to a poor Torah student. He should avoid sitting on a brand-new reed mat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new reed mat is still damp and has rough, sharp edges, so it damages clothing. This continues the theme of the last few steps: a student without much money must protect the few clothes he owns. Steps 21 and 23 already explained that decent clothing lets him keep a respectable place among people.

keyTerms.meaning: A student of the Torah academy (literally 'a son of the house of the רב')
On a mat (a woven reed mat)
Because it ruins or wears out

steps.confusionAlert: בַּר בֵּי רַב does NOT mean 'the son of a rabbi.' It is a standard phrase for a Torah student who learns in the בית מדרש. Also, מָאנֵיהּ here means clothing, not dishes.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּר בֵּי רַב לָא לִיתִּיב אַצִּיפְּתָא חַדְתָּא,
phrases.english: A Torah student should not sit on a new mat,
phrases.notes: A new reed mat is still damp and rough.

phrases.english: because it ruins his clothes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בַּר בֵּי רַב לָא לִיתִּיב אַצִּיפְּתָא חַדְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of רב חסדא's practical advice to students. This one adds a tip about protecting clothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Torah student should avoid sitting on a new mat because it damages his garments.

steps.title: A student should not give his laundry to his host
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא advises a student not to send his clothes to his host to be washed. The host might see something embarrassing and the student would lose respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: A Torah student should not send his clothes to his host to wash for him. That is not proper behavior, because the host might see something on them and the student will become disgraced.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives another tip about a student's clothing. This time it is about his dignity, not about money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A student who boards with a host might be tempted to hand over his dirty laundry. רב חסדא says this is not אורח ארעא, because the host might notice embarrassing stains (רש"י: signs of a seminal emission). The student would then be looked down upon, so he should wash his own clothes.

keyTerms.meaning: To his host (the person he lodges with)
To whiten it, meaning to wash it
To become disgraced or looked down upon

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּר בֵּי רַב לָא לִישַׁדַּר מָאנֵיהּ
phrases.english: A Torah student should not send his clothes
to his host to wash them for him,
because it is not proper conduct,
since perhaps he will see something on it
phrases.notes: רש"י explains this as signs of a seminal emission.

phrases.english: and the student will come to be disgraced.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בַּר בֵּי רַב לָא לִישַׁדַּר מָאנֵיהּ לְאוּשְׁפִּיזֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב חסדא's advice about a student's clothing. The concern shifts from protecting the clothes to protecting the student's dignity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student should not give his clothes to his host for washing, lest the host see something embarrassing and the student be demeaned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the section of advice to Torah students. It shows that a תלמיד חכם's personal dignity is a real concern, and that private matters should stay private.

steps.title: רב חסדא tells his daughters to be modest before their husbands
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells his daughters to behave modestly in front of their husbands. He gives an example: do not eat bread in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to his daughters: Be modest in front of your husbands. Do not eat bread in front of your husbands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from רב חסדא's advice to students to his advice to his own daughters. He opens with a general rule of modesty and gives a first example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general principle is צניעות, refined behavior in front of a husband. The example is not eating bread in front of him. רש"י explains that she might eat a large amount and look gluttonous, and lose some of his regard.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of (literally 'in the face of')

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to his daughters:
Be modest in front of your husbands,
do not eat bread in front of your husbands.
phrases.notes: רש"י says this is so she won't seem to eat excessively.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִסְדָּא לִבְנָתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from רב חסדא's advice to students to a new set of advice for his daughters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife should conduct herself modestly before her husband, for example by not eating bread in front of him.

steps.title: No vegetables, dates, or beer at night, and a separate bathroom spot
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא continues advising his daughters. They should not eat vegetables or dates or drink beer at night, and should not relieve themselves where their husbands do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not eat vegetables at night. Do not eat dates at night. Do not drink beer at night. And do not relieve yourselves where your husbands relieve themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא continues the list of tips for his daughters. All of them are about not becoming unpleasant to their husbands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vegetables at night cause bad breath. Dates and beer loosen the bowels, which would be unpleasant at night. Using a separate bathroom spot keeps the husband from being repulsed. Each tip is a practical way of carrying out the general rule of צניעות from the previous step.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's advice ends with two sets of tips. Students should protect their clothing and their dignity. His daughters should keep a refined, modest manner that preserves their husbands' affection.

phrases.english: Do not eat vegetables at night,
phrases.notes: They cause bad breath.

phrases.english: do not eat dates at night,
phrases.notes: Dates loosen the bowels.

phrases.english: and do not drink beer at night,
and do not relieve yourselves where your husbands relieve themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּיכְלוּן יַרְקָא בְּלֵילְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same speech to his daughters, adding more specific tips under the general rule of modesty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wives should avoid foods at night that cause bad breath or loosen the bowels, and should not share their husbands' bathroom spot.

steps.title: How to answer a knock at the door
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells his daughters to answer a knock with the feminine 'מני' (who is she?), not the masculine 'מנו' (who is he?).
steps.simpleTranslation: And when someone calls at the door, do not say 'מנו' (who is he?). Say 'מני' (who is she?).
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא keeps going with his modesty advice to his daughters. He tells them which word to use when someone knocks at the door.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a woman asks 'who is he?', it can sound like she expects a man to come visiting. Asking 'who is she?' shows she does not expect men to come calling. A small choice of words protects her good name.

phrases.english: And when a person calls at the door
do not say 'Who is he?'
phrases.notes: This is the word for asking about a man.

phrases.english: but rather 'Who is she?'
phrases.notes: This is the word for asking about a woman, so it doesn't sound like men come visiting her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי קָא קָארֵי אִינִישׁ אַבָּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of רב חסדא's modesty instructions to his daughters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Answer a knock with the feminine 'מני', not the masculine 'מנו'.

steps.title: The pearl and the clod of earth
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא showed his daughters a pearl right away but kept a clod of earth hidden until they were eager to see it. This taught that something hidden is more desired.
steps.simpleTranslation: He held a pearl in one hand and a clod of earth in the other. He showed them the pearl right away. He did not show them the clod until they were upset with curiosity. Then he showed it to them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא teaches his daughters a lesson about modesty by acting it out with two objects instead of explaining it in words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pearl is valuable, but because it was shown openly, it caused no excitement. The cheap clod of earth became something they badly wanted to see, only because it was hidden. The message is that what is kept modest and private becomes more precious.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's advice to his daughters ends with an acted-out lesson: concealment makes something more desirable, even if it is less valuable.

phrases.english: He held a pearl in one hand
and a clod of earth in the other hand.
The pearl, he showed them right away;
and the clod of earth, he did not show them
until they were upset from curiosity,
and then he showed it to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָקֵיט מַרְגָּנִיתָא בַּחֲדָא יְדֵיהּ וְכוּרָא בַּחֲדָא יְדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the series of רב חסדא's advice with an acted-out lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Something hidden is more desired than something shown openly, so modesty adds value.

steps.title: The vetches משנה does not follow one תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's rule about כרשינין and says the משנה does not follow a certain תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may not soak vetches.' Our משנה is not like this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier משנה about soaking כרשינין (vetches). It states that this משנה disagrees with a certain תנא, and the next step names him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That משנה forbids soaking vetches, but it still allows putting straw into a sieve. The גמרא points out that not everyone agrees using a sieve is allowed. The identity of the disagreeing תנא comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: soak in water (to separate the chaff)
vetches, a type of animal feed legume
not in accordance with this תנא

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The גמרא is jumping back to the משנה from before the long section on רב חסדא's advice.

phrases.english: The משנה said: One may not soak the vetches.
Our משנה is not in accordance with this תנא,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כִי הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic advice and returns to analyzing the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה, which allows a sieve, does not follow a certain תנא.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב forbids using a sieve entirely
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב forbids paying attention to a sieve at all on שבת. This is why the משנה does not match his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, one may not deal with a sieve at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for its claim. It shows which תנא disagrees with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets a person put straw into a sieve. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב forbids having anything to do with a sieve on שבת, probably out of concern that one will come to sift, which is a forbidden מלאכה. So the משנה cannot follow his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: as it was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
One may not deal with a sieve at all.
phrases.notes: The worry is that he might end up sifting or selecting, which is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that backs up the claim in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה does not follow a certain תנא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who forbids any use of a sieve on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה allows putting straw into a sieve. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב forbids the sieve completely, so the משנה does not follow him.

steps.title: New משנה: clearing feed away from an animal
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה records that רבי דוסא allows sweeping feed from before a fattened animal and moving it to the sides. The חכמים forbid this.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may sweep feed from before a fattened animal and move it to the sides because of the רעי. These are the words of רבי דוסא. The חכמים forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It presents a מחלוקת between רבי דוסא and the חכמים about clearing feed away from in front of an animal on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא allows this kind of light clearing of the feed, and the חכמים forbid it. The משנה gives no reason. The גמרא will later narrow the dispute to a trough that is a vessel (step 38), since sweeping a trough in the ground levels holes and is forbidden by everyone. The exact case of 'מפני הרעי' is explained in different ways.

keyTerms.meaning: dung, or (per רבינו חננאל) a grazing animal

steps.confusionAlert: The word רעי is read in two ways. One reading is 'dung', meaning the feed is moved away from it. The other, which follows רבינו חננאל, is 'an animal that grazes'. Do not get stuck here. The basic מחלוקת is simply whether you may clear feed aside.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may sweep hay from before a fattened animal
and move it to the sides on account of the רעי,
phrases.notes: רבינו חננאל reads רעי as an animal that grazes; others say it means dung.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Dosa;
and the Sages forbid it.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוֹרְפִין מִלִּפְנֵי הַפַּטָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a related subject: handling animal feed on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסא allows sweeping and moving feed aside before an animal; the חכמים forbid it.

steps.title: Moving feed from one animal to another
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one may take feed from in front of one animal and put it in front of another animal on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may take feed from before this animal and place it before that animal on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a simple rule. You may move food from one animal to another on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the disputed case of sweeping or clearing, this is just feeding an animal, so it is allowed. The גמרא will later look at whether this applies to every animal or only to certain ones.

phrases.english: One may take feed from before this animal
and place it before that animal on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹטְלִין מִלִּפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה זוֹ וְנוֹתְנִין לִפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה זוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second clause of the same משנה, giving a permitted case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moving feed from one animal to another on שבת is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: The new משנה has two parts. Clearing feed aside is a מחלוקת between רבי דוסא and the חכמים. Moving feed from one animal to another is simply permitted.

steps.title: Which part of רבי דוסא's ruling do the חכמים reject?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the חכמים disagree with the first clause of the משנה, the latter clause, or both.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They asked: Do the רבנן disagree with the first clause, or with the latter clause, or with both?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה with a question. It asks exactly how far the חכמים's disagreement with רבי דוסא goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא allowed two things: sweeping feed from before a fattened animal (the first clause), and moving feed to the sides, which also covers an ordinary animal (the latter clause). The משנה only says 'the חכמים forbid' without saying which part. So the גמרא wants to know whether they forbid one part or both.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a real open question)
The first clause of a משנה
The latter clause of a משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
A dilemma was raised before them:
Do the Rabbis disagree with the first clause,
phrases.notes: Sweeping feed from before a fattened animal.

phrases.english: or do they disagree with the latter clause,
phrases.notes: Moving feed to the sides, which also covers an ordinary animal.

phrases.english: or do they disagree with both?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבָּנַן אַרֵישָׁא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה quoted in steps 32–33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חכמים's prohibition covers the first clause, the second clause, or both clauses of רבי דוסא's ruling.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the חכמים forbid both cases
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the חכמים as forbidding moving the feed aside in both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: And the חכמים say: In both this case and that case, one may not move it to the sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows that the חכמים forbid in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'both this and that' mean the fattened animal and the ordinary animal alike. So the חכמים argue with both clauses of רבי דוסא's ruling, not just one.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is coming)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught:
And the Rabbis say:
both this one and that one —
phrases.notes: Feed before a fattened animal and feed before an ordinary animal.

phrases.english: one may not move it to the sides.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים disagree with both clauses. They forbid moving the feed aside for any animal.

steps.title: רב חסדא's first version: the dispute is about a ground trough
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the dispute is about a trough in the ground, and everyone permits sweeping a trough that is a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The dispute is about a trough in the ground, but with a trough that is a vessel, everyone agrees it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא limits where רבי דוסא and the חכמים argue. In this first version, the argument is only about a trough dug into the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A trough can be a hollow in the floor or a separate container. According to this version, sweeping a vessel trough is fine for everyone. The disagreement would then be only about the ground trough. The גמרא is about to question this.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the ground (dug into the floor)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The dispute is about a trough in the ground,
but with a trough that is a vessel —
everyone agrees it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בְּאֵיבוּס שֶׁל קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that the חכמים forbid both cases, רב חסדא defines what kind of trough the dispute concerns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First version: the dispute is about a ground trough, and a vessel trough is permitted by all.

steps.title: Who would allow sweeping a ground trough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that no one could allow sweeping a ground trough, because that levels holes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a trough in the ground — is there anyone who permits it? He is leveling holes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's first version. It asks how רבי דוסא could possibly allow sweeping a trough in the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sweeping a dirt floor fills in and smooths out holes. That is a forbidden מלאכה on שבת (like building or plowing). So it makes no sense to say רבי דוסא permits it, and the first version of רב חסדא cannot be right.

phrases.english: But a trough in the ground —
is there anyone who permits it?!
Why, he is leveling holes!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיבוּס שֶׁל קַרְקַע מִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּשָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's first version.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the dispute is about a ground trough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sweeping a ground trough levels holes, which is a forbidden מלאכה. So no תנא, including רבי דוסא, could permit it.

steps.title: רב חסדא's corrected version: the dispute is only about a vessel trough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates רב חסדא: the dispute is about a vessel trough, and everyone forbids a ground trough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רב חסדא said: The dispute is about a trough that is a vessel, but with a trough in the ground, everyone agrees it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by flipping רב חסדא's statement. Now the argument is only about a trough that is a separate vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel trough has no ground holes, so רבי דוסא can permit sweeping it. The חכמים still forbid it, most likely as a safeguard so people do not come to sweep a ground trough. Everyone agrees that a ground trough is forbidden because of leveling holes.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (a corrected version of a teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. The final version is the second one: the argument is about a vessel trough, and a ground trough is forbidden by everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: Ground trough: forbidden by all, because sweeping levels holes. Vessel trough: רבי דוסא permits and the חכמים forbid.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, this is how it was stated:
Rav Chisda said:
The dispute is about a trough that is a vessel,
but with a trough in the ground —
everyone agrees it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִי אִיתְּמַר הָכִי אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 37 by reversing רב חסדא's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrected version of the teaching (the statement is reversed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about a ground trough, and a vessel trough was permitted by all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about a vessel trough. A ground trough is forbidden by all because of leveling holes.

steps.title: Two ברייתות contradict each other on moving feed between animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about moving feed between animals and shows two ברייתות that give opposite directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one may take from before an animal.' One ברייתא taught: One may take from before an animal whose mouth is fine and give it to an animal whose mouth is foul. And another ברייתא taught: One may take from before an animal whose mouth is foul and give it to an animal whose mouth is fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about taking feed from one animal for another. It points out that two ברייתות seem to say opposite things, and it is setting up a resolution that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ברייתא allows moving feed only from a 'fine-mouthed' animal to a 'foul-mouthed' one. The other allows only the reverse. The exclamation at the end shows the גמרא sees a real contradiction that it must resolve.
steps.confusionAlert: The first line, 'וְנוֹטְלִין מִלִּפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה', is not a new teaching. It is just the גמרא quoting the משנה (from step 33) to show which line it is now discussing.

phrases.english: 'And one may take from before an animal.'
phrases.notes: A quote of the משנה's words.

phrases.english: One ברייתא taught:
One may take from before an animal whose mouth is fine
and place it before an animal whose mouth is foul.
And another ברייתא taught:
One may take from before an animal whose mouth is foul
and place it before an animal whose mouth is fine!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא חֲדָא: נוֹטְלִין מִלִּפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה שֶׁפִּיהָ יָפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the trough discussion to the next line of the משנה, quoted in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות explaining the משנה's rule about moving feed between animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא allows moving feed from a fine-mouthed animal to a foul-mouthed one, and the other allows the reverse. Both cannot be stated without explanation.

steps.title: אביי: Both teachings agree, donkey to ox only
steps.stepSummary: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying both ברייתות hold the same rule: feed may be moved from a donkey to an ox, but not from an ox to a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Both this ברייתא and that ברייתא agree. From in front of a donkey to in front of an ox, we may take the feed. From in front of an ox to in front of a donkey, we may not take it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction from the last step. He says the two ברייתות do not really argue, because both agree on one direction of moving feed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות only looked opposite because of how they were worded. אביי gives the actual rule both of them share: moving feed from a donkey to an ox is allowed, and moving it from an ox to a donkey is not. Next, he will show how each ברייתא's wording points to this same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that. Here it means both ברייתות agree.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי is picking one ברייתא and rejecting the other. He is saying both teach the same rule in different words.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for moving feed on שבת. The direction matters: donkey to ox is allowed, ox to donkey is not.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Both this and that (baraita agree)
From before a donkey to before an ox
We take (the feed);
phrases.notes: Allowed.

phrases.english: From before an ox to before a donkey
We do not take.
phrases.notes: Not allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the two ברייתות raised in step 39.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: both sources share one rule and differ only in wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות give opposite directions for moving feed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both allow donkey to ox and forbid ox to donkey.

steps.title: Explaining 'fine mouth' and 'foul mouth' in the first teaching
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the first ברייתא's wording. The 'animal with a fine mouth' is the donkey, because it has no saliva. The 'animal with a foul mouth' is the cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for what it teaches: 'One may take from before an animal whose mouth is fine.' That means a donkey, because it has no saliva. 'And one may give before an animal whose mouth is foul.' That means a cow,
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now shows how the first ברייתא's wording fits his rule. He explains which animal each description refers to. The explanation continues past the end of this passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A donkey's mouth is called 'fine' because it has no saliva, so the feed left in front of it stays clean and can be given to another animal. A cow is the 'foul-mouthed' animal, and it is the one receiving the feed. This fits אביי's rule that feed goes from the donkey to the ox or cow.

phrases.english: And that which is taught:
"One takes from before an animal whose mouth is fine"
Refers to a donkey, which has no spittle.
phrases.notes: So the leftover feed stays clean.

phrases.english: "And one places before an animal whose mouth is foul"
Refers to a cow,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּקָתָנֵי נוֹטֵל מִלִּפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה שֶׁפִּיהָ יָפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies אביי's rule from step 40 to the wording of the first ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא's descriptions as specific animals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Fine mouth' and 'foul mouth' seemed to conflict with the other ברייתא's terms.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fine mouth means the donkey, which has no saliva. Foul mouth means the cow.
